raw_text:
name: dotnet-csharp-source-generators

Creates/consumes Roslyn source generators: `IIncrementalGenerator`, syntax providers, semantic analysis, diagnostics, `CSharpGeneratorDriver`, `[GeneratedRegex]`, `[LoggerMessage]`, STJ `[JsonSerializable]`, and NuGet analyzer packaging. See [skill:dotnet-roslyn-analyzers], [skill:dotnet-csharp-modern-patterns], and [skill:dotnet-csharp-coding-standards].

Source generators are shipped as analyzers targeting `netstandard2.0`.
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
<TargetFramework>netstandard2.0</TargetFramework>
<EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>true</EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>
<IsRoslynComponent>true</IsRoslynComponent>
<LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers" Version="3.3.4" PrivateAssets="all" />
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp" Version="4.12.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
> **Always target `netstandard2.0`.** Generators load into the compiler process, which requires this TFM for compatibility. Use `LangVersion>latest` to write modern C# in the generator itself.
Always use `IIncrementalGenerator` over the legacy `ISourceGenerator`. Incremental generators are cache-aware and only re-run when inputs change, making them significantly faster in IDE scenarios.
1. **Filter early** -- Use `ForAttributeWithMetadataName` or `CreateSyntaxProvider` with a tight predicate to minimize
2. **Transform to simple data** -- Extract only the data you need (strings, records) in the transform step. Never pass
`ISymbol` or `SyntaxNode` through the pipeline (they hold the compilation alive and break caching).
3. **Use value equality** -- Pipeline outputs are compared by value. Use `record struct` or implement `IEquatable<T>`
for custom types.
4. **Emit deterministic output** -- Same inputs must produce identical source. Use `// <auto-generated/>` and
`#nullable enable` headers.
Report errors and warnings through `SourceProductionContext` rather than throwing exceptions.
> **Scope note:** This example targets top-level, non-generic classes for clarity. A production generator should also handle generic type parameters and nested types. Report a diagnostic for unsupported shapes rather than emitting invalid code.
**File naming convention:** `{TypeName}.{Feature}.g.cs`
Use `RegisterPostInitializationOutput` for marker attributes and helper types that do not depend on user code.
Use `CSharpGeneratorDriver` to run generators in-memory and verify output.
For more robust testing, use the [Verify.SourceGenerators](https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.SourceGenerators) package.
Compile-time regex generation. Zero runtime compilation cost, AOT-compatible. Method must be `static partial` returning `Regex`; place on `partial class` (or `partial struct`).
High-performance structured logging with zero-allocation at log-disabled levels. Methods must be `static partial` in a `partial class`. `Exception` parameter is logged automatically (do not include in message template).
AOT-compatible JSON serialization. Eliminates runtime reflection. Register all types that need serialization in `[JsonSerializable]` attributes. Use `TypeInfoResolverChain` (net8.0+) to combine multiple contexts. Required for Native AOT -- reflection-based serialization is trimmed.
<ProjectReference Include="..\MyGenerator\MyGenerator.csproj"
When shipping a generator as a NuGet package, place the assembly under `analyzers/dotnet/cs/`:
<IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>
<DevelopmentDependency>true</DevelopmentDependency>
<None Include="$(OutputPath)\$(AssemblyName).dll"
PackagePath="analyzers/dotnet/cs" />
Add `Generated/` to `.gitignore`.
